newsitem.title: GERMANY: Gehe plans to sell pharma production units.
newsitem.headline: Gehe plans to sell pharma production units.

text.p: German pharmaceutical wholesaler Gehe AG on Tuesday said it plans to sell its pharmaceutical production units to focus on expanding the wholesale business.
The sale is expected to earn Gehe 1.2 billion marks. The pharmaceutical production units last year contributed about three percent to Gehe's total group sales of 19.2 billion marks.
Gehe said in a mandatory statement it plans to sell its German units Azupharma GmbH, Aliud Pharma GmbH & Co. KG and allphamed Arzneimittelgesellschaft mbh as well as French unit GNR-pharma S.A.
The company was not immediately available for comment on the buyers of the four units.

On Monday German daily Handelsblatt reported that Swiss drugs giant Novartis, to be formed through the merger of Sandoz AG and Ciba Geigy AG, would buy Azupharma while German group Stada AG would buy Aliud.
German chemicals giant BASF AG has already agreed to purchase GNR.
Gehe management board chairman Dieter Kaemmerer said the sale would free up resources to concentrate on expanding the group's global position as a leading drugs wholesaler.
Similarly by spinning off almost all drugs production units, Gehe would remove any possible conflicts of interest in its wholesale business.
Gehe is still battling U.K. group UniChem Plc to take over Lloyds Chemists.
